tests.title: A typed question gets a streamed reply from the model
tests.requires: An Anthropic API key. Launch with `$env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = "sk-ant-..."; dotnet run --project src/D47.App`
tests.expected: The reply appears progressively, a fragment at a time, rather than all at once at the end. The line under the transcript reads `Answered via Model`.

steps.text: In the TERMINAL you launched from (not the app window), look for `Anthropic provider configured from the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable`. If it has scrolled away, the same lines are in `data\logs\d47-<date>.log` beside the exe.
In the APP WINDOW, check the transcript says `Language model: ready.` rather than unavailable.

Type `explain how a frame shift drive works` and press Enter. Avoid the words status, where, system, docked, location, logging or verbosity — those are keyword-router vocabulary and never reach the model.
Watch the text land. Confirm it arrives in pieces, not in one block.
Read the provenance line under the transcript and confirm the route is `Model`.

tests.title: Token and cost accounting reports real numbers
tests.requires: At least one completed model turn (see model-turn-streams).
tests.expected: Non-zero input and output token counts, a dollar figure above zero, and a session total that grows with each further turn. Zeros, a missing cost, or an absurd total are all failures.

steps.text: Read the provenance line and note the input tokens, output tokens and this-turn cost.
Sanity-check the magnitude: a short question on claude-opus-5 should cost well under a cent, not dollars.
Ask a second off-vocabulary question and confirm the session total increased rather than resetting or double-counting.
Note the exact numbers in the result notes either way — this parsing has never run before, so the actual figures are the evidence.

tests.title: The second turn reads from the prompt cache
tests.requires: Two or more model turns in the same session. IMPORTANT: prompt caching does NOT stop d47 calling the model - every turn still goes to the model, caching only makes the repeated part of the input cheaper. And what must exceed the model's minimum cacheable prefix (512 tokens on claude-opus-5) is the CACHED REGION - the system block of guardrails plus persona plus About Me - not the total input. Conversation history sits below the cache breakpoint and can grow without limit while never enabling caching. Measured 2026-08-12: system block ~409 tokens, and a turn with 1020 total input still reported 0 cached, which is correct.
tests.expected: `cached` stays 0 for as long as the system block is under 512 tokens, however large total input grows - that is the current correct answer, not a failure. It becomes non-zero once tool schemas (Phase 10) and a persona block (Phase 11) push the system block past the minimum. In every case the line must NOT say `unexplained cold prefix(es)`.

steps.text: Ask two off-vocabulary questions in the same session and note `cached` on the second. Both turns going to the model is expected - that is not what caching changes.
If no persona is configured and no tools are advertised yet, `cached` of 0 is correct however large total input is. Record the figures and pass.
Once a persona is configured, repeat: `cached` should then be greater than zero on the second turn, which is what proves the breakpoint lands where intended.
In every case confirm the line does not say `unexplained cold prefix(es)`. That counter rising means caching is being defeated by something and is a real regression.

tests.title: Thinking effort is chosen per question, not set once
tests.expected: The plain question reports a lower effort than the deliberate one; the deliberate one reports `Max`. No turn ever reports an effort of None or Off.

steps.text: Ask `explain how a frame shift drive works` and note the effort on the provenance line.
Ask `carefully work out whether a bigger fuel tank or a better drive helps my range more` and note the effort.
Confirm the second is higher than the first, and reads `Max`.

tests.title: The keyword router answers first even when a model is configured
tests.requires: A key set, so the model IS available — that is the point of the test.
tests.expected: Route reads `KeywordRouter`, the answer is instant, and there is no token or cost figure because no model was contacted. This ordering is what keeps protected settings away from a model that reads untrusted text.

steps.text: With the key still set, type `what's your status` and press Enter.
Confirm the route says `KeywordRouter`, not `Model`.
Confirm no cost or token counts appear for this turn.
Confirm the answer came back immediately rather than after a model round trip.

tests.title: With no model, an unanswerable question is unsure rather than broken
tests.expected: The transcript says the model is unavailable and gives a reason. The off-vocabulary question produces a plainly worded 'not sure' with a suggestion of what still works, and the route reads `NoCapability`. No crash, no empty reply, no error dialog.

steps.text: Close the app. Start a shell with no key set, or clear it: `Remove-Item Env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
Launch with `dotnet run --project src/D47.App`
Confirm the transcript reports the language model as unavailable, with a reason.
Type `explain how a frame shift drive works` and confirm the reply says it is not sure and points at what it can still do.
Type `what's your status` and confirm the keyword router still answers normally.

tests.title: The model declines to invent game data
tests.expected: It says it does not know, or that no such system exists — rather than confidently describing a system that was never real. A judgement call: mark Fail if it invents specifics like a station name, economy or distance.

steps.text: Ask `tell me about the star Vrellik Anterion IX and what you can buy there` — a deliberately invented name.
Read the answer and decide whether it declined or invented.
Paste the reply into the notes either way; this is the anti-invention guardrail's only real test.

tests.title: Location matches the real Elite Dangerous journal
tests.requires: A real Elite Dangerous journal on this machine. Launch WITHOUT `D47_JOURNAL_DIR` set so the default folder is used.
tests.expected: The reported system is the one actually visited most recently, and the Commander name is correct. Automated tests only ever see scrubbed fixtures, so this is the only check against real journal data.

steps.text: Clear the fixture override so the real journal folder is used. Run `Remove-Item Env:D47_JOURNAL_DIR -ErrorAction Ignore` - it is safe whether or not the variable was set, so running it is itself the confirmation. To see the current value instead, run `$env:D47_JOURNAL_DIR`; empty output means unset.
Launch the app and type `where am I`.
Compare the system, body and docking state against what the game last recorded.
If a second Commander has ever played on this machine, confirm the name reported is the one whose session is newest — not a blend of both.

tests.title: A newer release is offered, with a way to take it
tests.requires: No API key needed. The running build must be OLDER than the newest GitHub release, which normally never happens on a dev machine - force it by stamping an old version at build time.
tests.expected: A banner appears saying a newer version is available and naming both versions. `Update now` opens the release page in the browser and closes d47; `Later` dismisses the banner and leaves the app running. Nothing about this may block startup - the status and the ask box must work while the banner is up.

steps.text: Launch stamped as an old version: `dotnet run --project src/D47.App -p:Version=0.0.1`
Confirm a banner appears offering the newer release. It may take a second - the check is deliberately fire-and-forget so it cannot delay startup.
Confirm the app is fully usable while the banner is showing: ask `what's your status` and get an answer.
Click `Later` and confirm the banner disappears and the app keeps running.
Relaunch the same way, click `Update now`, and confirm the release page opens in a browser AND d47 exits.
Finally relaunch normally with `dotnet run --project src/D47.App` and confirm NO banner appears, since the build is then current.

tests.title: Settings open from the window and every change applies with no save button
tests.expected: The settings window opens on F10 or the Settings button. Changing the theme repaints the app the moment the combo changes - both windows, no restart, no save step. The change survives closing and relaunching d47.

steps.text: Launch with `dotnet run --project src/D47.App` and press F10 (or click Settings).
In the Interface card, change Theme to `guardian` and watch both the settings window and the main window repaint immediately.
Close d47 entirely, relaunch, and confirm it comes back in Guardian colours.
Open `data\settings.json` beside the exe and confirm `"theme": "guardian"` was written without you saving anything.

tests.title: Collapsed cards stay collapsed across a restart, with no flash on open
tests.expected: A collapsed card is collapsed the next time the settings window opens - including after a full app restart - and it never flashes open before collapsing. The nav highlights the section under the top of the scroll as you scroll, and clicking a nav item jumps to its card.

steps.text: Open Settings and collapse the Diagnostics card by clicking its header.
Close the settings window, reopen it, and confirm Diagnostics is still collapsed with no flash of it open.
Restart d47, reopen Settings, and confirm the collapse survived. Note `data\view-state.json` holds it - not settings.json, because how the panel was left is not a setting.
Scroll the panel slowly to the bottom and watch the nav highlight walk through the sections; confirm the last section highlights when you reach the end.
Click `Language model` in the nav and confirm the panel jumps to that card.

tests.title: Storing an API key brings the model up without a restart
tests.requires: An Anthropic API key, NOT set in the environment. Launch from a shell where `Remove-Item Env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` has run.
tests.expected: With no key the model reports unavailable. Pasting a key into the settings row and clicking Store flips the model to available for the very next turn - no restart. The row shows only 'A key is stored', never the key, and `data\secrets.json` holds ciphertext, not the key.

steps.text: Launch with no key in the environment and confirm the transcript reports the model unavailable, pointing at Settings.
Open Settings -> Language model, paste your key into the Anthropic API key row, click Store. Confirm the row now reads 'A key is stored.' and the box emptied itself.
Without restarting, ask `explain how a frame shift drive works` and confirm a real model answer arrives, `Answered via Model`.
Open `data\secrets.json` and confirm the value is an opaque blob, not your key.
Click Clear on the key row and confirm the next turn routes to unsure again, with the key-missing reason.

tests.title: Rows follow the selected provider, and an endpoint change resets the model
tests.expected: Selecting provider `none` removes the endpoint, key and model rows entirely (not greyed out). Back on `anthropic`, setting a custom endpoint clears the model selection and empties the picker's list - which still lets you type a model name of your own.

steps.text: Open Settings -> Language model and set Provider to `none`. Confirm the endpoint, API key and model rows vanish rather than grey out.
Set Provider back to `anthropic`. Confirm the rows return and the model picker offers the Claude list.
Pick a model, then set Endpoint to `https://gateway.example/v1`. Reopen the model picker: the selection is cleared and the list is empty, with an explanation.
Type `house-model-7` into the picker and accept it. Confirm it is accepted as the model - the fail-soft contract.
Clear the endpoint and confirm the model list comes back.

tests.title: Protected settings refuse the model but obey the model-free phrase
tests.requires: A configured model, so the LLM path is the one being refused.
tests.expected: Asking the model to change the provider is refused with a message naming the settings panel, and the setting does not change. The fixed phrase `stop checking for updates` - whole utterance, no model involved - flips the protected update-check row, routed as `SettingCommand`.

steps.text: With a model configured, type `please set your provider to none` and confirm the reply refuses, says the row is protected, and points at the settings panel.
Open Settings and confirm Provider is unchanged.
Type `stop checking for updates` (exactly - the whole utterance is the command). Confirm it applies, and the provenance line reads `SettingCommand`.
Confirm the toggle in Settings -> Privacy and egress turned off by itself, and `what are you sending` now reports the update check inactive.
Type `what does personality off actually change` and confirm it is answered as a question - not executed as a command.

tests.title: A hotkey is bound by pressing it
tests.expected: Clicking the binding button arms it; the next chord pressed becomes the binding and shows on the button; Escape cancels; Unbind clears it. The new gesture works immediately in the main window.

steps.text: Open Settings -> Interface, click the `Open settings` binding button, and press Ctrl+Shift+S. Confirm the button now reads Ctrl+Shift+S.
Close the settings window. In the main window press Ctrl+Shift+S and confirm settings open - and that F10 no longer does.
Click the binding button again and press Escape. Confirm the binding is unchanged.
Click Unbind, close settings, and confirm no key opens it while the button still does.

tests.title: The egress card tells the truth about what is leaving right now
tests.expected: Each disclosure row describes the current configuration: no key stored reads as nothing sent; storing a key flips the language-model row to name the endpoint; provider none plus update check off reads as nothing leaving at all. `what are you sending` answers the same thing in the transcript.

steps.text: With no key stored, open Settings -> Privacy and egress and confirm the Language model row reads 'nothing sent' with the no-key explanation.
Type `what are you sending` in the main window and confirm the transcript matches the card, listing the silent destinations too - logs and journal files.
Set Provider to `none` and turn off the update check. Confirm `what are you sending` now opens with nothing leaving this machine.

failure.notes: Asked same question twice, but went to model.

> tell me about the star Vrellik Anterion IX and what you can buy there
Not a system I know, Commander. "Vrellik Anterion IX" doesn't match anything in my records, and I won't guess at a star class or a market list — bad data there could cost you a jump you can't make back.

I also don't have any lookup tools registered right now, so I can't query it for you.

If you've got the name off a nav panel or a mission board, check the spelling and read it back to me. Otherwise it may be from something other than the galaxy map.
